traveller: Marco Polo: Venetian man with warm light-olive skin, dark brown wavy hair, long straight nose and dark brows. At departure age17: slim, clean-shaven, simple brown wool tunic and muted rust cloak. During eastern travel age18–24: lean build and short dark beard emerging. In China age25–36: short dark beard, plain practical belted Yuan-period travel robe in muted brown or blue-grey, no royal insignia. At sea and home age37–44: weathered face, dark beard beginning to grey, practical travel clothes. Father Niccolo and uncle Maffeo are distinctly older bearded merchants, never Marco duplicates. Clothing adapts to climate. No European Renaissance hats or Qing queues.

scenes.title: Taking the western road
scenes.caption: Kublai sent Marco on a mission to the far south-west, probably around 1277. At Zhuozhou he took the western road, which he said ran for ten days through Cathay past fine cities, vineyards and mulberry groves.

composition.view: Three-quarter rear view Marco23 riding small horse with Yuan guide onto dusty road toward distant western hills, cultivated plain and low village, no repeated main-route fork composition.

evidence.passage: Book II: the mission to the west; Juju.

scenes.title: Vineyards at Taiyuan
scenes.caption: At Taianfu, now Taiyuan, he noted vineyards, which he said were the only ones in the province of Cathay, and plenty of wine. The city also made weapons and equipment for the Khan's armies.

composition.view: Close vine-level view bunches of modest grapes on wooden trellis, Shanxi cultivated valley behind and ceramic harvesting basket, no European chateau or modern wire vineyard rows.

scenes.title: Silk merchants in Pingyang
scenes.caption: At Pianfu, now Pingyang, he found a great city of merchants and craftsmen, with much silk. Carts and pack animals carried such goods west along the road toward Xi'an.

scenes.title: Across the Yellow River
scenes.caption: Beyond a castle he called Caichu, he reached the Caramoran, the Yellow River, too wide and deep to bridge. He crossed by boat into a country of ginger, silk and game.

scenes.title: Ropes and river mud
scenes.caption: Yellow River ferries had to cross a heavy, silt-laden current. Ferrymen worked them with long sweeps and ropes, and the crossings were kept running as stations on the Khan's post roads.

scenes.title: Outside Prince Mangala's palace
scenes.caption: At Kenjanfu, now Xi'an, he found Kublai's son Mangala ruling as prince from a great palace outside the city walls. Mangala died in 1280, which helps date Marco's journey to before then.
scenes.prompt: Oblique approach modest Yuan princely palace outer courtyard near Xi'an, tiled timber hall over low rammed-earth platform and mounted officials, no Ming city wall gate or ForbiddenCity.

scenes.title: Through the Qinling valleys
scenes.caption: From Xi'an the road took twenty days through the Qinling, a country of mountains and valleys whose forests were full of 'lions', bears, lynx and deer. By lions he meant tigers.

scenes.title: A bridge lined with shops
scenes.caption: At Sindufu, now Chengdu, he described rivers half a mile wide flowing through the city, crossed by stone bridges. Each bridge had a wooden roof, painted red, on marble columns.

scenes.title: Under the bridge roof
scenes.caption: Along each bridge, he wrote, were rows of booths where merchants plied their trades, taken down at night. The Khan collected a toll on the goods that crossed.

scenes.title: Bamboo in the campfire
scenes.caption: In Tebet, a country laid waste by Möngke's wars, travellers burned green canes at night. Heated, the canes burst with such a bang that lions, bears and other beasts fled, and horses not used to it bolted.

scenes.title: The lake at Caindu
scenes.caption: In Caindu, around modern Xichang, he described a lake that produced pearls, which the Khan did not allow to be fished freely in case they lost their value. A mountain there yielded turquoise, also reserved for the Khan.

scenes.title: Salt cakes used in exchange
scenes.caption: Instead of coins, people in Caindu used salt: brine boiled down and pressed into cakes, stamped with the Khan's mark. Eighty cakes, he said, bought a saggio of gold.

scenes.title: Gold in the river gravel
scenes.caption: He crossed a great river he called the Brius, in which, he said, gold dust was found in great quantity. It is the upper Yangtze, whose Chinese name, Jinsha, means 'golden sand'.

scenes.title: The market at Yachi
scenes.caption: At Yachi, now Kunming, he found a great city of merchants and craftsmen, home to Muslims, Nestorian Christians and Buddhists. He noted that people ate meat raw, chopped and seasoned.

scenes.title: Shells as money
scenes.caption: In Yunnan, he wrote, money was white cowrie shells from the sea, eighty to a saggio of silver. Cowries stayed in use in Yunnan for centuries, long after paper money had spread through the rest of China.

scenes.title: The old kingdom of Dali
scenes.caption: Beyond Yachi lay Carajan, the old kingdom of Dali beside Erhai lake, which Kublai himself had conquered in 1253. He described great serpents ten paces long, with jaws that could swallow a man: crocodiles.

scenes.title: Horses of the south-west
scenes.caption: Carajan bred large, fine horses, sold as far as India. He noted that its riders used long stirrups, like the French, and docked a joint of their horses' tails so they could not lash the rider.

scenes.title: The road beyond Yongchang
scenes.caption: At Zardandan, around Yongchang, he found people who covered their teeth in gold. Near here, he wrote, the Khan's horsemen had beaten the King of Mien and his war elephants; the History of Yuan dates the battle to 1277.
